clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1: every chain 999 result of cycles 9 to 19 that read state at a past block, which endpoint answered, and whether the clearance in state/cleared.json that cites it holds. Method: all scripts in cycles/009 to cycles/019 work directories that call eth_call, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getBalance, eth_getCode or eth_getTransactionCount with a block number and mention chain 999 or one of its endpoints (31 files), and all 75 chain 999 clearances of those cycles that name a block, a replay or a census.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On 2026-11-25 a batch to https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm ('hyperliquid evm Mainnet') returned 24,009 bytes of PoolManager code at block 10,000,000, long before deployment, while https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31) returned 0x at the same block and both gave block hash 0x433762ce...d629 for it. So the official endpoint answers past-block state from head, as the unit says. The cited state endpoint lists hold: cycles/011/theme-mined-liquidity.work/lib.py:12-15 sets STATE_URLS 999 to drpc only, cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/common.py:18-19 sets STATE 999 to drpc and purroofgroup, and cycles/013/theme-swap-residuals.work/raw/r2-999.json records stateUrls drpc and hyperlend. The official endpoint appears in those files only for logs and receipts (common.py:21 RECEIPT), which do not depend on a state tag. The audit covers cycles 9 to 19; a quick read of cycles 4, 5 and 7 found their chain 999 state reads at latest with overrides (005/theme-claim-operators.work/state.py:41-44) or on the archive node (007/hyperevm.work/equalbal.py:5,42), so no earlier clearance rests on head state either.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3: the shapes of #81868 (C1: an 8, 16 or 32 bit value shifted by a constant), #79182 (C2: shift left by 63 or 31, flagged when the operand is x + x, x * 2 or x << 1) and #81689/#81668 (C3: make of a slice with a non-constant length) added to the cycle 18 shapescan and run over holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and v1.2.4 and the core/vm, core/state, core/types, trie, rlp and common/math trees of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2, coreth and graft/evm of avalanchego 1.15.3, libevm d398bc4dbe41, nitro geth 0e44603 and Celo op-geth c7ed55b8. A positive control file with the issue 79182 reproducer gives C1, C2 (dbl=true) and C3.
clearedSpotChecks.note: bor v2.11.1 core/vm/analysis_legacy.go (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1) holds setN at lines 38-45 with b := byte(a >> 8), a uint16 shifted by an untyped constant, as the unit says. I ran my own jump destination test with eth_call and a code override: PUSH2 to PUSH16 with 0x5b push data, 0 to 7 leading PC bytes, a jump to the PUSH opcode, to every data byte and to the real JUMPDEST after it, 120 cases sampled with seed 7 (19 must succeed, 101 must fail). BNB Chain https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104 go1.26.10) and Avalanche https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc (avalanchego/1.15.3 go1.26.10) gave the specified outcome on all 120. Polygon https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1 go1.26.10) put batches behind a Cloudflare challenge and rate limited single calls during this check; one single call returned 'invalid jump destination' for a jump into PUSH2 data, as specified, and the rest of the Polygon sample was not run by me. The unit's own out/t3_setn-1-137-43114.json records 1,620 cases with no mismatch on five bor builds. The compiled form of setN was not read by me either, which the unit leaves as a low lead.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2: which forno backend answers past-block state reads. eth_getCode, eth_getBalance and eth_getStorageAt(slot 0) of the PoolManager at blocks 43,985,162, 60,000,000, 75,046,581, 83,000,000 and latest, each in its own pinned three element batch, up to 60 tries per read until both backends answered.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On 2026-11-25 twelve pinned three element batches [web3_clientVersion, eth_getCode(PoolManager, block 60,000,000), web3_clientVersion] to https://forno.celo.org were all answered by reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb with 24,009 bytes, and a pinned read at block 40,000,000 (before deployment at 43,985,162) returned 0x from reth, so the past-block answers honour the tag. Six pinned reads at latest came from both backends (one Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8, five reth). This matches the unit's routing result, so the cycle 18 historical results on forno came from celo-reth. Routing is a load balancer setting that can change; the result holds for the reads made, not as a guarantee.
